articles.title: Amazon’s online car ‘dealership’ with Hyundai is now live
articles.summary: Amazon is now selling vehicles through its website for the first time. The company has a deal with Hyundai to feature dealer models in 48 cities in the US.
articles.body: Today, for the first time, you can buy a car — yes, a whole car — on Amazon. Same-day delivery not guaranteed. The e-commerce giant’s first foray into car shopping is called Amazon Auto. The company is partnering with Hyundai dealers in 48 cities in the US to list vehicles on the site. Customers can browse, order, find financing, and arrange delivery — all within the familiar confines of Amazon’s online ecosystem. Of course, if you’re looking for anything other than a Hyundai, you’re out of luck. At least for now. “With Amazon Autos, we’re bringing the simplicity and ease customers expect from Amazon to car shopping, one of their largest purchases, while offering dealers a new channel to connect with a broad audience,” Fan Jin, global head of Amazon Autos, said in a statement. “We’re excited to have Hyundai as our exclusive launch partner and look forward to welcoming more brands and expanding our selection to customers as the program grows.” Amazon first announced its plans to get into car buying last year, Previously, customers could browse car showrooms and compare prices on Amazon — but not actually buy a car. With the partnership with Hyundai, Amazon has finally added a key piece of the puzzle. And importantly, the end seller of the vehicle is still the dealer; Amazon’s platform will be the middleman between the customer and the dealership. As such, Amazon needs to appeal to dealers almost as much as it does to car shoppers. The company is making its pitch by arguing that it can offer “a new sales channel that connects them with millions of Amazon customers.” And with over 310 million active users, Amazon certainly has the numbers to back it up. Trade-ins will also be accepted through Amazon’s new car vertical. Customers will have to answer a series of questions about the conditions of the vehicle, after which the request will be processed by an “independent valuation service” to determine the value of the trade-in. [Image: A list of the 48 US cities where Amazon can sell you a car. And for a limited time, Amazon is sweetening the deal by offering a gift card for $2,300 for anyone who buys a car through the site. The card can be applied to the vehicle purchase, but the offer ends on January 10th, 2025. People typically hate car shopping, with most surveys showing that the dealership experience tops people’s lists of frustrations. Tesla has helped spearhead a movement toward a direct-to-consumer (DTC) model in which people buy their vehicles directly from the company, eschewing a dealership. Forty-eight states have laws that limit or ban manufacturers from selling vehicles directly to consumers — though that has started to shift recently thanks to Tesla’s popularity. Tesla has no independent dealerships, but dealership associations in multiple states have filed numerous lawsuits against Tesla to prevent the company from selling cars. Amazon’s deal with Hyundai neatly sidesteps this issue by ensuring that dealers remain a crucial part of the process. Most dealers allow customers to browse and buy a car through their own websites, but having Amazon as an additional platform with millions of daily customers is sure to help make the process even easier.

articles.title: 'Dancing With the Stars' has delivered some fierce fashion in Season 35. We asked kids to rate the best looks.
articles.summary: We asked eight kids, ages 4 to 11, for their opinions on Season 35 fashion. "Too much skin" came up.
articles.body:
Season 35 of Dancing With the Stars has given us so much: Perfect 10s and triumphant tangos. A 10 Things I Hate About You reunion . And so, so many sequins and feathers. As the season heads into Nov. 24's finale, we asked eight kids, ages 4 to 11, what they make of the bold looks that have sashayed across the ballroom.

There have been coconut bras and sheer gowns ("No," a 7-year-old said of one undie-exposing dress). Disney Night and the Halloween theme brought up some beloved characters, and some creepy ones too. Alfonso Ribeiro gets a lot of love from Gen Alpha — even if his suits don't.

If you thought the DWTS judges were tough, just see what some of these pint-sized critics have to say. Let's give them the floor …

"The Minions would eat them." — Gigi, 11

"I love it, but I wouldn't wear it because it's showing her tummy." — Lily, 6

"No. You can see her undies!" — Jolie, 7

"Weird. Wait, is that Alfonso?" — Beau, 8

"Razzle dazzle, as my mom says!" — Eva, 11

"It's Tinkerbell and Captain Hook. I love this one. Her dress is so cute and light and flowy." — Gigi, 11

"Perfect — and the golden cage is pretty." — Eva, 11

"Tinkerbell fairy and pirate. I like her." — Zaya, 5

"Beauty and the Beast! I love her yellow dress. But wait, I thought when the Beast turned back to human, he lost the horns?" — Gigi, 11

"It looks just like the characters!" — Eva, 11

"Belle has a golden costume and Beast has a fluffy one. How did he get horns?" — Zaya, 5

"Oh my gosh! Is it actually Belle and Beast? I love Belle's dress! I was her for Halloween when I was 3 and my 1-year-old brother was the Beast!" — Lily, 6

"He has a beautiful, what's that, a hoodie?" — Zaya, 5

"It looks like they are at a dancing rodeo." – Eva, 11

"Looks like they're playing a skipping game. La la la la la la." — Gigi, 11

"They look like oranges on an island." — Eva, 11

"She also looks like Moana, and he looks like Flynn Rider and both are wearing the same pants." — Zaya, 5

"Is her whole shirt a flower?" — Lily, 6

"It is a fall celebration and she looks like Moana." — Zaya, 5

"I didn't know that Guillermo was into the hula." — Eva, 11

"Wow. I don't know what his message is, but one day I'll understand." — Gigi, 11

"Both of them are concerningly underdressed." — Gigi, 11

"I like sparkly black pants, but his are also good even though it's not sparkly." — Zaya, 5

"Looks like she is the middle of a rose." — Eva, 11

"Gives Elphaba when she's defying gravity." — Gigi, 11

"Are they actually carrying her?" - Lily, 6

"Her dress is sooo long that peoples have to carry her dress." — Zaya, 5

"Are they supposed to be clowns? Wait, they're barefoot?" — Oliver, 8

"Insanely awkward creepy clowns whose clothes don't fit." — Eva, 11

"Joker and girl Joker." — Zaya, 5 "They look scary!" — Lily, 6

"That doesn't even scare me!" — Leo, 4 (Lily's little brother)

"She looks good for a fashion party. He looks good for a pajama party." — Jolie, 7

"It works for a crazy Christmas outfit, I guess." — Jolie, 7

"She looks like Moana too. Everyone looks like Moana! And he looks like a tap shoe dancer." — Zaya, 5

"They look like leopards that are showing off." — Eva, 11

"She has my favorite color and her shoes are beautiful and her earrings are beautiful and I also like the boy 'cause he is also wearing my favorite color." — Zaya, 5

"Hawaii beach party. Party at the beach!" — Gigi, 11

"Look like they are on vacation." – Eva, 11

"She has flowers and beautiful shoes. He has Mexican flag." — Zaya, 5 (It's the Irish flag, but she got two of the three colors right.)

"Is that Alfonso Ribeiro? I know him from Funniest Home Videos ." — Oliver, 8

"He looks like he is the ocean." — Eva, 11

"Looks like mean divas that would be in Mean Girls ." — Eva, 11

"They look like Gomez and Morticia!" — Lily, 6

"I didn't know you could bleed diamonds. I want to try." — Eva, 11

articles.title: Amazon Autos is coming to the UK.
articles.summary:
Amazon first launched its Autos business in the US almost two years ago, and now it’s expanding across the pond in early 2027. The UK will be the first country outside the US to get access to Amazon Autos, with Hyundai the first announced launch partner. Brits will be able to browse Amazon’s dealer inventory and get instant trade-in valuations, and Amazon says more car brands will be announced “ahead of launch.”

articles.title: Actress Rishita Kothari's boyfriend Mridul Meena defends her amid Avinash Mishra-Eisha Singh controversy; says ‘I know my girl’
articles.summary: Amid the ongoing controversy surrounding television actors Avinash Mishra and Eisha Singh’s reported fallout, Rishita Kothari’s name has also been dragged
articles.body: Amid the ongoing controversy surrounding television actors Avinash Mishra and Eisha Singh’s reported fallout, Rishita Kothari’s name has also been dragged into the discussion. Now, her boyfriend, Mridul Meena, has come forward to defend the actress and requested fans to stop involving her in the matter. Through a note shared on Instagram, Mridul urged social media users to respect their privacy and refrain from creating unnecessary assumptions about Rishita.In his note, Mridul made it clear that neither he nor Rishita wished to become part of the ongoing discussion. He also emphasised that they preferred to maintain silence out of respect for everyone’s personal lives.Mridul’s note read, “A humble request to everyone: Please don’t drag Rishita into the ongoing controversy or involve us in it. We prefer to stay silent out of respect for everyone’s personal lives.”He further addressed fan pages that have been discussing the actress and creating narratives around her alleged involvement. Reiterating his support for his girlfriend, Mridul wrote, “I also request fan pages not to create unnecessary narratives or assumptions. Let’s respect everyone’s privacy and allow everyone, including us, to live peacefully. And no matter what, I know my girl. I will always stand by Rishita and support her whenever needed.”Rishita’s name surfaced amid speculation surrounding Avinash Mishra and Eisha Singh’s relationship. The two actors, who developed a close bond after meeting on Bigg Boss 18, recently sparked breakup rumours after fans noticed that they had unfollowed each other on social media.Soon after, allegations of Avinash allegedly being unfaithful to Eisha began circulating online, with Rishita’s name also getting linked to the speculation. However, these claims have not been independently established, and neither has there been any confirmed evidence of Rishita’s involvement.Avinash Mishra apologises amid the ongoing controversyAmid the growing discussions, Avinash shared a video addressing the situation and apologised for his actions. While he did not directly confirm the cheating allegations, he took responsibility for the separation and acknowledged that his actions had hurt Eisha and her family.In the video, Avinash said, “Bahut saare meanings nikale jaa rahe hai, edits ban rahe hain. I know yeh sabse zyada Eisha aur uske family ko hurt kar raha hai. Mera aisa koi intention nahi tha, but joh bhi hua hai uske liye. I am sorry. Hum jo alag bhi hue hai uske liye bhi, if there is anyone to blame, it’s me. Meri hi galti hai vahan pe bhi.”He further requested people not to involve their families and friends in the matter, adding, “I am here just to apologise and say ki family aur friends ko involve na karein. This is not how it should be. Main request karunga aap logon se ki iss cheez ko yahan pe end karein. Koi iss cheez ko badhaye na because do logon ki cheez hai.”Meanwhile, Eisha’s close friend Rajat Dalal had also shared a video making allegations against Avinash and accusing him of cheating on the actress. Eisha, too, had hinted at having evidence that she could share if required.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tidal will remove every fully AI-generated song from December 9, deleting 29 million tracks and blocking new ones from being uploaded
articles.summary: Tidal is clearing fully AI-generated music off its platform.
articles.body: Tidal is clearing fully AI-generated music off its platform. Starting December 9, the streaming service will reject any new track made entirely with AI tools and begin removing the roughly 27 million already sitting in its catalog. Robert Anderson, who heads Tidal at parent company Block, expects the count to reach 29 million by the time the clean-up ends at the start of 2027, with 80,000 to 85,000 uploads turned away every day after that.The ban reaches beyond direct uploads. Distributors, the companies that deliver music from artists to streaming services, can no longer send such tracks, and Tidal will reject any delivery whose metadata says a song came solely from AI. Anything that slips through will be checked by Ircam Amplify, Tidal's AI detection partner. Songs made with the help of AI can stay, and only those that are the sole output of tools like Suno and Google's Lyria will go."Something more drastic needs to be done," Anderson wrote on X, calling Tidal the first streaming service to take this step and urging rivals to "follow suit."Nearly half of all new uploads on Tidal are now made by AIThe numbers behind that decision climbed quickly. Over the past 90 days, 43% of all tracks delivered to Tidal were wholly AI-generated, and on November 6, the share crossed 60% in a single day. Most of it traces back to one tool, with Suno responsible for 94% of the tracks carrying Tidal's AI badge.Listeners have largely ignored this music. Those 27 million tracks make up 6.3% of the catalog, yet 96% of them have not been streamed even once in the last three months. Tidal's argument is that they do damage simply by being there. "At this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried," the company said, while conceding that some songs need time to find an audience.Some of this music is also built to deceive. Tidal has already pulled over 65,000 tracks flagged for posing as real artists, a practice it says "diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans."Cutting royalties for AI music was not enough to stop itThe ban arrives five months after Tidal's first attempt at the problem. Its AI policy, effective June 29, cut fully AI-generated tracks out of the royalty pool, and by mid-July listeners started seeing an icon next to them. AI music linked to fraud, from fake artist uploads to unusual streaming activity, was blocked outright.Taking away the money was supposed to take away the reason for mass uploads. The uploads kept climbing anyway, and Anderson said that is what pushed Tidal to remove the tracks altogether.Spotify and Apple Music still let fully AI-generated songs inThat puts Tidal well ahead of the two biggest platforms on this issue. Spotify tags AI-generated artist profiles as "AI Persona" and keeps them out of its editorial and algorithmic recommendations, and said in October it had pulled around 50 million spam tracks from recommendations this year. At the same time, it is working with Universal Music Group on a paid feature that lets Premium users make AI remixes and covers of songs. Apple Music has said it will label AI-generated and AI-assisted tracks.Neither has banned fully AI-made songs. Bandcamp, the music marketplace popular with independent artists, did so in January. On Tidal, the removals start on December 9.Fearless legend or grounded realist? Rate yourself on 11 categories in the Great Indian Confidence Survey – find out in 3–6 min

articles.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage
articles.summary: Microsoft has declared a Code Red internally, after a massive Outlook outage in November. Engineering teams are now focused on resolving outages much sooner.
articles.body: This month’s Exchange Online and Microsoft Outlook outage has prompted the software giant to declare an unusual “Code Red” internally, Reuters reports. The nearly 24-hour outage took down email for millions of customers, and was triggered by a bug that had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers since July without any impact to servers. In a memo to the teams responsible for Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 Core president Jason Henderson revealed the outage was the most significant in history for Microsoft’s customers. “Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday,” said Henderson. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team.” As part of this Code Red declaration, Microsoft is focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning, and faster recovery mechanisms. Microsoft now has a target of resolving future outages within an hour, and will reportedly deploy AI agents to help engineers diagnose issues. Microsoft is now holding daily meetings with the engineering group responsible for Microsoft 365 services, alongside weekly reviews. In a separate memo, Amanda Silver, Microsoft’s corporate vice president of M365 Core and Work IQ, said engineers had to work through a “fog of war” to help resolve the outage. I reported last week that Microsoft engineers had a running bridge call during the entire outage, and at one point it hit the maximum of 1,000 participants. Microsoft engineers had to exchange messages across 11 Teams chats and reportedly “struggled ​to maintain a cohesive picture” during the outage because of the fragmented internal tracking systems. Sources tell me the outage was marked as “sev0,” the highest level, which indicates a catastrophic level of service disruption. Engineers struggled to get servers back online because they had entered maintenance mode and became unresponsive due to unusually high CPU loads.
